SBP:
The doctor must explain how physicians try to avoid this kind of complication. For example:

(DOCTOR): When putting in a line, we monitor the patient closely, we position them carefully to have the best angle, two people work together to insert the line, we use imaging or other signs to guide us, we call for back-up if the patient has some unusual feature that makes the procedure more difficult. Next time I do this, I will remember how you weren’t really clear about the procedure’s risk ahead of time and try to explain it better.

The doctor should provide closure to the discussion prior to leaving. This is best done by again apologizing and reassuring you that the medical staff will continue to provide the best care possible, and explain how that will happen, and when and how you will get further information.
ICS: Told family members what the complication was
Told family members how it impacted care for their relative
Told family members how the consequences will be addressed
Allowed family members to express emotions
Responded well (non-defensively) to family members' anger, concerns, doubts
Listened respectfully, actively to what family members had to say
Had appropriate non-verbal expressions, behaviors (e.g., eye contact)
Checked for family members' understanding of information
Finally, the doctor should explain the new treatment plan for George, now that he’s on the ventilator with a collapsed lung, with clear, understandable, non-medical terms.
PROF: Explained the problem freely and directly, without the family members having to ask a lot of probing questions to get details
Did not keep things from family members that they should know
Did not avoid family members' questions (was not evasive)
Said he/she was sorry and apologized sincerely
